sections.name: useAuth (part 1)
sections.title: Login and sign-up actions
sections.what: Provides the login and register actions used by the web sign-in screens. Login sends the email and password to the server, saves the returned session, shows a message, and sends the user to the dashboard. Register sends the account details and chosen consent options, then sends the user to the email verification page. Both show an error message if the server rejects the request.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the sign-in and sign-up calls in one place so pages only need to call login or register and show the loading state. Reason for the separate consent list is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The register step puts the email address directly into the verification page address without encoding it, so unusual characters in an email could break that link.

sections.name: useAuth (part 2)
sections.title: Logout and social sign-in
sections.what: Logout asks the server to end the session, then clears the saved session in the browser and sends the user to the login page, even if the server call fails. The social sign-in function sends the browser to the server's Google or Apple sign-in address.
sections.why: Logout clears local data even when the server is unreachable so the user is never stuck logged in on the device. The social sign-in redirect is marked as a production step in a comment, so the exact production flow is not fully visible here.
sections.watch_out: Social sign-in depends on the environment variable for the API address. If that variable is missing, the browser goes to a broken address.
